scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Para Para emerged in the early 1980s, with theories suggesting it began with VIP room staff choreographing moves to impress clients or from the Takenoko-zoku subculture in Harajuku.
The term is onomatopoeic, mimicking the sound of hand movements to music.
on_screen: Map: Japan · East Asia
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Para Para is performed at club events, anime conventions, and as a social activity.
It serves as a way to engage with specific Eurobeat tracks, which often have unique, dedicated routines.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage: File:Parapara dance 2009 France.webm (https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/23/Parapara_dance_2009_France.webm?utm_source=commons.wikimedia.org&utm_campaign=imageinfo&utm_content=original)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Dancers perform synchronized arm and hand movements to a four-on-the-floor beat.
Footwork is minimal, consisting of side-to-side steps, hip sways, and occasional hops.
Routines are divided into intro, melos, and sabi sections.
Watch for Sabi choreography.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (nah1-LwkJGQ)
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Synchronized group formation, usually facing forward.
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The dance is primarily set to Eurobeat, a fast-paced electronic genre derived from Italo disco.
Other variants use hyper techno (TechPara) or trance (TraPara).
Listen for the Synthesizer, Drum machine, Electronic keyboard.
The pulse is 4/4 at about 150 beats a minute.
Fast-paced, high-energy electronic music characterized by driving synth melodies and a steady, rhythmic kick drum.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Historically associated with Japanese club culture, including venues like Maharaja, Twinstar, and Velfarre.
Costumes vary by era, often reflecting the fashion of the time, such as the gyaru style during the third boom.
on_screen: Image gallery: 2 licensed images with attribution
Reconstruction imagery allowed only from the costume notes, labelled 'reconstruction'

scenes.title: The people
narration: Key groups include Shishō Gundan, T-RREX, Team SEF, and the ParaPara Allstars, who were instrumental in the commercial spread of the dance.
TechPara (hyper techno) and TraPara (trance) are the most prominent variants, differing in speed and complexity of movement.
Para Para is linked to the Takenoko-zoku subculture and shares stylistic similarities with traditional Bon Odori, though a direct historical link is debated.
